title: Teleoperation of Kuka Robotic Arm | Software Engineer
content: I led a team of three in developing an integrated virtual reality system designed to enhance user control and precision in teleoperating robotic arms. This system, implemented in the Monash Smart Manufacturing Hub's Digital Twin Lab, enables intuitive real-time manipulation of a KUKA robotic arm using VR hand-tracking and an advanced two-finger haptic feedback glove. Working every day for three months over the summer, we achieved significant milestones. Haptic Glove I designed and tested seven iterations of the glove, sourced components, created the electrical schematic, soldered and crimped connections, and wrote Python scripts on a Raspberry Pi Model 4B to enable two-way communication with the robotic arm gripper. Additionally, I designed the housing for the Raspberry Pi. The haptic glove now functions seamlessly upon power-up.   Robotic Arm I wrote the KUKA Sunrise Java code that allows the robotic arm and end effector to receive values from the server, enabling real-time control. This required an in-depth understanding of OPC UA to create new variables, as well as extensive research into KUKA Sunrise and Robotiq Gripper 2F-140 documentation. Ultimately, I successfully integrated the gripper with both the KUKA robotic arm and the server. VR & Hand Tracking I developed the virtual lab environment that users interact with in VR. Additionally, I wrote C# scripts that track the user's hand, calculate movement differences, and transmit the data to the server for the robotic arm to mimic. I also wrote scripts for mapping gripper movement in Unity and learned how to integrate different robotic frames. Furthermore, I co-wrote the locomotion scripts that allow users to navigate the lab and authored the view-changer script, which lets users switch between different perspectives.     Camera Streams I sourced and implemented a Zed Camera, RealSense Camera, and LogiCamera, integrating them with a Xavier Jetson to enhance teleoperation by making control more immersive and intuitive.   Software Development My contributions extended to software development, where I wrote the code that connects the KUKA robotic arm to the server, implemented OPC UA for industrial communication, and developed the Unity-based control system for the gripper. Additionally, I engineered the hand-tracking system, calculated movement differences, and transmitted them to the server while integrating all camera streams for a seamless operator experience. Administration I formed and led the team, holding weekly meetings with our supervisor and bi-weekly meetings with the team. I also wrote all the necessary documentation to obtain ethics approval, including the Explanatory Statement, Consent Form, Interview Topics, and Survey Questions - ensuring we could conduct testing with participants. Additionally, I authored and secured approval for two detailed risk assessments, one for the project as a whole and another specifically for the full-body haptic suit, assuming the role of Risk Owner. I conducted extensive academic research in this field, developed a six-month project timeline (Gantt Chart), and contributed significantly to the project report.       Ultimately, this project was highly rewarding. By reducing cognitive strain and improving operational accuracy, we laid the groundwork for future advancements in haptic-enhanced teleoperation. title: Autonomous Driving | ML Engineer
content: I developed a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict vehicle steering for autonomous driving, enabling my robot to navigate both urban and rural roads. The model processed RGB camera images to generate real-time steering commands, incorporated stop sign detection, and dynamically adjusted speed based on road conditions. After extensive data collection, training, and deployment on a Raspberry Pi-controlled robot, I secured 1st place in the Need4Speed Challenge at RVSS 2025, demonstrating exceptional performance in autonomous navigation and real-world adaptability. title: Olympics Database | Data Engineer
content: I developed a robust database system for Paris Arrow Transit (PAT) to manage transportation logistics for events like the Olympics. I worked across both relational and non-relational databases, leveraging SQL, PL/SQL, and MongoDB to build a flexible and efficient system. My work involved not only creating and populating the database to meet specified requirements but also implementing advanced features such as sequence management and data integrity enforcement through triggers and stored procedures. I restructured the schema to accommodate new business rules, including managing official roles and handling complaints about drivers' behavior. The system was designed to automatically suspend drivers based on accumulated demerit points and ensure that all trip-related data adhered to business logic. Additionally, I integrated MongoDB to handle driver-trip data in JSON format, adding another layer of scalability to the project. Throughout, I ensured that the database was efficient, scalable, and aligned with future needs. Github Repository    Github Page (Demo)

title: Library Data | Data Engineer
content: I designed a comprehensive database system for the ReadMore Community Library (RCL), which serves Local Government Agencies (LGAs). The database manages information related to LGAs, their branches, and the managers overseeing them. It ensures efficient data storage and retrieval while maintaining data integrity through normalization. By creating detailed conceptual and logical models, and implementing them into a functional database schema, I streamlined RCL's operations. I learnt the importance of well-structured databases in managing large-scale organizational data. Github Repository    Github Page (Demo)

title: Australian Earthquakes Analysis | Data Analyst
content: I  explored seismic activity across Australia from 2008 to 2024, highlighting key events, trends, and their impacts. By analyzing earthquake data, I identified regions with higher seismic activity, such as Western Australia, and examined the relationship between earthquake magnitude, depth, and resulting damage. The analysis emphasizes the importance of understanding earthquake risks for informed infrastructure planning, particularly in regions near active tectonic boundaries. This project showcases data visualization techniques and provides valuable insights into Australia's lesser-known earthquake activity. Github Repository    Github Page (Demo)

title: Australian Athletes Analysis | Data Analyst
content: Developed an interactive visualization that explores Australia's Olympic performance from 1900 to 2024. Built using Tableau, this dashboard provides a comprehensive analysis of athlete participation, medal counts, and trends across different Olympic events. Users can explore historical data to uncover patterns in Australia's sporting success, compare performances across decades, and analyze the impact of various factors on medal achievements. With dynamic charts, filters, and insights, this tool serves as a valuable resource for sports analysts, historians, and enthusiasts looking to understand Australia's Olympic legacy in a visually engaging way. title: Garbage Shooter | Game Developer
content: I created an interactive game designed to simulate space waste management, raising awareness about environmental issues related to human waste in space. This project aimed to engage users in a fun way while educating them on the importance of proper space waste management. The game works by having the user control a spaceship, moving it left and right using the arrow keys, and shooting lasers to destroy incoming space debris with the space bar. As the user progresses, the debris moves faster and in greater quantities. They earn points for every piece of debris destroyed. Github Repository
